question: Who was the better scorer: Kobe in 2005-06 or Curry in 2015-16?

# Scoring Claim Review

## Answer

**Split scoring verdict: the selected rate-and-efficiency measures do not support one winner.**
The advantages below depend on the metric or phase. Choosing an overall winner would require an additional priority, rather than a conclusion established by these data.
Claim assessment: Conditional: the broad claim is not uniformly supported across the selected metrics.
**Regular Season: Kobe Bryant leads total points, points per game; Stephen Curry leads true shooting, league-relative efficiency.**
**Playoffs: Kobe Bryant leads points per game; Stephen Curry leads total points, true shooting, league-relative efficiency.**

**Scope:** 2005-06–2005-06 versus 2015-16–2015-16; Regular Season, Playoffs.

## Key evidence

- **Regular Season / Points per game (per game)**: Kobe Bryant **35.4**; Stephen Curry **30.06**. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=977&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- **Regular Season / Raw true shooting (%)**: Kobe Bryant **55.89**; Stephen Curry **66.94**. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=977&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- **Playoffs / Points per game (per game)**: Kobe Bryant **27.86**; Stephen Curry **25.11**. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=977&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)

## What changes the interpretation?

- The playoff raw true shooting comparison favors Stephen Curry; the playoff-minus-regular-season change favors Kobe Bryant. A higher playoff level is not the same as a larger change from the regular season. Different games and opposition prevent a causal interpretation. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=977&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- The playoff points per game comparison favors Kobe Bryant; the playoff-minus-regular-season change favors Stephen Curry. A higher playoff level is not the same as a larger change from the regular season. Different games and opposition prevent a causal interpretation. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=977&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- Playoffs: the accumulated points comparison favors Stephen Curry; the points per game comparison favors Kobe Bryant. Accumulation and scoring rate answer different questions. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=977&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)

- **Postseason Changes for Bryant**: Bryant's scoring volume decreased from 35.4 to 27.9 PPG (-7.5 PPG), while his shooting efficiency rose across all metrics (e.g., TS% up from 55.9% to 58.7%) (ev_4644ce5416c811281c8c, ev_5e9cbd1cb9a6ee84fe81).

- **Coverage Limitations**: Statistics reflect official NBA box scores and tracking for the specified seasons only; playoff sample sizes differ notably (7 games for Bryant, 18 games for Curry) (ev_cb0dafc54bd55b5f6d19, ev_9e4eb0b715452dbdc3e2).
